To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the new CLSI interpretive breakpoints for ceftazideme result in high rates of ceftazidine susceptibility among CTX-M-producing Enterobacteriacae; 2) CTX-M-13-producing E. coli have higher MICs than wild-type strains; 3) ceftazidme is not a reliable agent for the treatment of serious infections due to these organisms.
the new CLSI interpretive breakpoints for ceftazideme may lead to the underestimation of ceftazidine resistance in some CTX-M-producing strains.
high rates of susceptibility to cefazidime were found among CTX-M- producing E. coli isolates, which may be clinically relevant, given the lack of clinical outcome data.
